recommendation: Keep this no-change audit. Future Subscription edits should preserve the distinction between notification transport, Bundle.entry.request metadata, and Subscription resource create/update interactions.
issue_request: FHIR-19957 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I change request for FHIR-core Subscription, raised against STU3 and applied for R5. It asked to resolve confusing Subscription text that mixed generic post/posting language with REST-hook guidance suggesting payload-bearing notifications should be sent as an Update operation/HTTP PUT.
initial_application: No commit explicitly names FHIR-19957, but the issue appears to have been applied during the R5 Subscription redesign. Commit 3be1bbb7 updated source/subscription/subscription-notes.xml after the July 2019 vote, replacing the old full-payload REST-hook sentence that told servers to forward matching resources as an Update operation (PUT) with wording that describes create, update, or delete operation metadata inside the notification bundle. FHIR-23738's R5 placeholder comment later explicitly listed FHIR-19957 as clarified at subscription.html#rest-hook, saying REST-Hook uses HTTP POST.
additional_context: Subscription, SubscriptionStatus, and SubscriptionTopic are active current-build resources in source/fhir.ini. The current REST-hook source states that clients use rest-hook to receive notifications via HTTP/S POST and that the server POSTs a notification Bundle to the client's endpoint. The broader Subscriptions Framework separately says clients may request the Subscription resource via HTTP POST or HTTP PUT under normal FHIR create/update rules, so create/update of the Subscription resource is no longer conflated with outbound notification delivery. Zulip R5 Feedback discussion recorded the FHIR-19957 rest-hook clarification as part of the merged R5 Subscription work, and Confluence search found no contrary work-group record.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current source already conveys the reconciled R5 rule and does not retain the old direct Update-operation/PUT framing for payload-bearing REST-hook notifications.
